clusters.snippet: A recent brightening turned out to be from a star orbiting inside another.

clusters.text: A recent brightening turned out to be from a star orbiting inside another. In the Andromeda Galaxy, a giant star about seven times as massive as the Sun spent nearly a decade slowly swallowing its much smaller companion. The process, known as common envelope evolution, was proposed in the 1970s to explain how some of the tightest pairs of stars in the Universe form, but no one had ever caught it in the act. In a new Nature study, astronomers led by Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University, finally witnessed the entire spectacle from the decades before it began to the eruption that ended it in late 2025. “It lasts for a few years, maybe a few decades,” Karambelkar said. “Stars evolve on time scales of millions of years. So, it’s really like a blip on the entire cosmic time scale.” Some pairs of stars orbit so close to each other that they could not have formed at that distance, so their orbits must have shrunk. Common envelope evolution is the leading explanation for that shrinkage. When one star in a binary grows old, it expands into a giant, and its outer layers can engulf its companion. The two then share a single, loosely bound envelope of gas. As the engulfed star drags through it, it loses orbital energy to friction and spirals inward. Depending on how much of the envelope gets lost, the pair either ends up in a much tighter orbit or merges. Karambelkar’s team spotted a candidate system where this might be happening while searching Andromeda for stars changing in brightness, using the Wide-field Infrared Transient Explorer (WINTER) telescope at Palomar Observatory and data from NASA’s Near-Earth Object Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (NEOWISE) mission. One giant had been brightening for seven years. “When a star first swallows its companion, it has a very subtle effect on its brightness,” Karambelkar said. “It slowly brightens, and a lot of light comes out in the infrared.” In April 2025, Karambelkar’s team published a paper suggesting that this system, named AT 2025abao, was undergoing an engulfment in progress. Back then, though, they couldn’t rule out a competing explanation: a single star with instabilities deep within its core. So, they kept watching. Rob Bonta, the US state’s attorney general, issued the subpoena as part of an investigation into whether exports of the California-based company’s advanced semiconductor chips ended up in China, contravening US restrictions. “The conduct of Nvidia and its former chief executive raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the company may have misled investors,” said Bonta. “Nvidia is in a messy, transnational situation but the underlying principle of our corporate securities law is clear: companies cannot mislead their investors.” The subpoena, issued on Thursday, followed Huang’s resignation a week ago after it emerged he had multiple affairs, including one with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy. Bonta said the investigation would also look at whether the former Nvidia chief’s actions resulted in confidential information being passed to China. “My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang’s actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information,” he said. “And if Nvidia misled investors and the public about this risk, in violation of the law.” Nvidia’s shares are down by a fifth since Huang admitted the extramarital affair, hitting a one-year low at the close of trading on Thursday, and wiping almost $1tn off its market value. Earlier this week, Harvey Jones, Nvidia’s chair, said the company had no intention of reinstating Huang after the former CEO said he would be “honoured” to return. clusters.text: NASA's Voyager 1 has phoned home from one light-day away, marking humanity's first emissary to cross this monumental threshold way out in interstellar space. Flight controllers received the spacecraft's call Thursday, exactly 24 hours after it was sent. That's how long it took for the radio signal to traverse the more than 16 billion miles at the speed of light. "Voyager 1 light-day distance confirmed ... Voyager 1 continues its journey into the unknown," controller Nshan Kazaryan announced to cheers and applause. For a spacecraft already loaded with historic firsts, it was an especially momentous milestone. "Once again Voyager breaking records, breaking boundaries and taking humanity on a voyage," NASA's science mission chief Nicky Fox said. "There's no end for the Voyager mission." Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 swept past Jupiter in 1979 and Saturn in 1980, snapped the most distant photo ever taken of our "Pale Blue Dot" in 1990, became the most distant human-made object in 1998, and crossed from the sun's sphere of influence into the vast void between stars in 2012. NASA could not confirm the newest distance record until the signal reached the control team at California's Jet Propulsion Laboratory via the deep space telescope near Madrid. But that didn’t stop the space agency from wishing everyone a "Happy Voyager light-day … day!" via social media on Wednesday. Voyager 2 actually beat its twin into space by two weeks. But its route to Jupiter and Saturn, plus Uranus and Neptune, was slower and longer, and it did not reach interstellar space until 2018. It won't reach the one-light-day mark until 2035. Both spacecraft are doing well for their 49 years of age, plowing through space at 38,000 mph with plutonium for power. Picture-taking ended long ago, but they typically send back bits of precious data almost every day on their never-before-explored environment. clusters.title: Prayagraj's Rs 12,000 Crore Metro Plan Expands To 70 Km And 45 Stations, Track Work Likely Next Fiscal
clusters.text:
Prayagraj is preparing for a major overhaul of its public transport, with officials finalising a 70-km metro network and large maintenance depots at Jhunsi and Cheoki.

The project, estimated to cost over Rs 12,000 crore, is expected to enter the construction stage soon as route feasibility studies near completion.

First planned under the Smart City mission as a 44-km light metro with 39 stations, the project has been upgraded to a full metro system with 45 stations to cope with the city's growing population and traffic congestion.

Prayagraj Development Authority (PDA) vice-chairman Rishi Raj said the route and feasibility surveys for the expanded network are almost complete, and track laying is scheduled to begin in the next financial year.

The metro will run three-coach trains on two main corridors, one linking Bamrauli with City Lake in Jhunsi and the other connecting Shantipuram to Cheoki. Parade Ground has been proposed as the central interchange station.

The corridors will improve access to key areas including Sulemsarai, the airport zone, Sangam and Naini. In the first phase, the Bamrauli to Jhunsi line will have 20 stations, while the Shantipuram to Cheoki line will have 19.

With 30 to 35 km of the planned route passing through military areas, officials are preparing a special plan and seeking mandatory clearances from the Army.

Two maintenance depots of 14 hectares each, covering over 28 hectares in all, will be set up at Khanupur in Jhunsi and on Army land in Cheoki.

Since more than 14 hectares of the depot land belongs to the Army, the PDA has formally asked the district administration to arrange alternative land in exchange.

According to PDA engineers, land for the depots has been identified and construction is likely to start within the next few months.

clusters.title: Drunk drivers can’t start Prayagraj’s new Volvo e-buses
clusters.text: Prayagraj: Travel by bus operated by UP State Road Transport Corporation (UPSRTC) is all set to become safer as the new Volvo electric buses in the city will not allow a driver to start the vehicle without clearing a breath analyser test. The driver will have to undergo a breath test before starting the bus and only if the reading is normal will the operating system activate, allowing the bus to move. The buses, equipped with advanced safety technology developed by Russian company RG Mobility, are expected to start operations soon.The buses also come equipped with a black box-like recording system, which will make it easier to establish how an accident occurred and determine the circumstances leading to it. A special camera installed near the front windshield will continuously record activity ahead of the bus. The footage will be stored both on the bus and at the control room, with backups at both locations available for analysis after an accident.The Russian company’s electric buses are running in Uttar Pradesh, but the Volvo models have been given only to Prayagraj for now. Kanpur will get them in the second phase.These UPSRTC buses have five additional CCTV cameras apart from the main camera. One of these will monitor the driver and help establish whether the driver was using a mobile phone while driving. The other cameras will monitor passenger activity inside the bus.Passenger safety has also been given special attention. A hammer has been placed near the window of every seat so that passengers can break the glass and escape in an emergency. Four fire extinguishers have been installed in each bus, while two special buttons near the driver’s seat can be used to alert the system in case of fire.Each seat has two emergency buttons. One will send a signal to the driver to stop the bus, while the other is an SOS button that can be pressed by any passenger, including women, during an emergency. The alert will be transmitted to the control room for immediate assistance.The buses have been registered with Regional Transport Office (RTO), and their operation in Prayagraj is expected to begin shortly, said Ravindra Singh, regional manager, UPSRTC, Prayagraj.Stay updated with the latest Prayagraj news.
